cards.title: What are articles?
cards.body: *a*, *an*, *the*: small words before nouns. Czech has none, so articles are the number-one English problem for Czech speakers at every level.
cards.body_cz: *a*, *an*, *the*: krátká slova před podstatnými jmény. Čeština je nemá, a proto jsou členy problém číslo jedna pro Čechy na každé úrovni.
points: They are not optional. Every singular countable noun needs one: ~~I have dog~~ → *I have **a** dog.*
They tell the listener which thing you mean: any one, the one you both know, or things in general.
Czech carries that signal by word order: *Na stole je kniha* (new: **a** book) / *Kniha je na stole* (known: **the** book). English word order is fixed, so the article does the work instead.

cards.title: The three choices
cards.body: Before every noun, one of three: *a/an*, *the*, or nothing. The choice depends on what the listener knows.
cards.diagram_fallback: NOUN takes one of three: a / an (any one, new: I saw a dog.) · the (we both know which: The dog barked.) · zero (in general: Dogs bark.)

table.caption: the three
rows: one of many · new to the listener · a job
we both know which · only one exists · superlatives · fixed cases
plurals and uncountables in general · most names · meals · *in hospital, at school*

points: Cards 3 to 7: the meaning decides. Cards 8 to 12: the pattern decides.

cards.title: First mention, then known
cards.body: New to the listener: *a/an*. After that, you both know which one: *the*. No particular one in mind: nothing.
cards.diagram_fallback: FIRST MENTION a / an -> KNOWN the -> IN GENERAL zero · I saw a dog. The dog barked. Dogs bark. · She sent an email. The email was short. Emails are quick.
points: *the* also works without a first mention when the listener can work out which one: *Can you close **the** door?*
~~I bought the new phone yesterday~~ (new information) → *I bought **a** new phone yesterday.*

cards.title: General vs specific
cards.body: The most common B1 error. Things in general take no article; a particular one takes *the*.
cards.body_cz: Nejčastější chyba na úrovni B1. Obecně platné věci nemají člen; konkrétní věc má *the*.

table.caption: general vs specific
rows: ***The** life of a nurse is hard.*

points: ~~The life is hard~~ → *Life is hard.* ~~I like the dogs~~ (in general) → *I like dogs.*
Test: can you add *in general*? No article. Can you say which one? *the*.
Czech has one form for both: *život* is *life* and *the life*. English makes you choose every time.

cards.title: Places: the activity or the building
cards.body: *hospital, school, bed*: no article for the activity that happens there; *the* for the building or the place itself.
points: *at work* has no building meaning: always *He's **at work**.*
Czech *v nemocnici* covers both. English splits it: ~~She's in the hospital~~ (a patient) → *She's **in hospital**.*

cards.title: Meals
cards.body: Meals work like places: the meal as an event takes nothing; a particular meal you describe takes *the*.

table.caption: meals
rows: ***The** breakfast at the hotel was good.*

points: ~~I had the breakfast at eight~~ → *I had breakfast at eight.*
With an adjective, *a* returns: *We had **a** lovely dinner.*

cards.title: Jobs and roles
cards.body: A job is one of many: *a/an*. A role only one person holds: *the*.
points: ~~I am teacher~~ → *I am **a** teacher.* Czech speakers drop this one at every level.
Test: could another person have the same job at the same time? Then *a/an*.

cards.title: Countries
cards.body: Most countries take no article. *The* goes with names that contain a common noun (*republic, kingdom, states*) or a plural.
points: ~~I live in Czech Republic~~ → *I live in **the** Czech Republic.* ~~She's from the France~~ → *She's from France.*

cards.title: Geography names
cards.body: Names on a map follow a pattern, not a meaning. Learn the pattern.

table.caption: on the map
rows: seas and oceans: *the Atlantic Ocean, the Baltic Sea*

points: Famous buildings usually take *the*: *the Eiffel Tower.*
~~I swam in Danube~~ → *I swam in **the** Danube.* ~~We climbed the Mount Everest~~ → *We climbed Mount Everest.*

cards.title: Names on the calendar
cards.body: Months, days, years and festivals are names: no article, like cities. Parts of the day take *the*.
points: The error comes from English, not Czech: *in the morning* and *in the summer* get stretched to months. ~~in the August~~ → *in **August**.* ~~on the Monday~~ → *on **Monday**.* ~~in the 2019~~ → *in **2019**.*
Two fixed exceptions: *at **night***, no article; *at **the** weekend*, always *the*.
*the* returns when you say which one: *on **the** Monday after Easter*, *in **the** summer of 2019*. Seasons alone take either: *in summer* / *in the summer*.

cards.title: Nationalities and languages
cards.body: *The* + nationality means the people as a group. The language takes no article.
points: ~~English love tea~~ → ***The** English love tea.* ~~I study the English~~ → *I study English.*

cards.title: Always the
cards.body: Some nouns take *the* every time: there is only one, or the pattern is fixed.

table.caption: always the
rows: *the sun, the moon, the sea, the internet*

points: ~~I play piano~~ → *I play **the** piano.* ~~He's best player~~ → *He's **the** best player.*
*the news* is one thing, not many: *The news **was** surprising.*

cards.title: Which article?
labels: A name on the map or the calendar, or a fixed case?
the pattern: the Danube · Prague · August · the piano
In general: any, all, or the activity?
zero: Dogs are friendly · in hospital · breakfast
Do you both know which one, or is there only one?
the: the dog next door · the sun · the best
One thing: a / an. Some things: nothing. a dog · dogs · a teacher
cards.diagram_fallback: 1. A name on the map or the calendar, or a fixed case? -> use the pattern: the Danube, Prague, August, the piano, the news. 2. In general: any, all, or the activity? -> zero: Dogs are friendly, Life is hard, in hospital, breakfast. 3. Do you both know which one, or is there only one? -> the: the dog next door, the sun, the best. 4. Otherwise: one thing a / an, some things nothing: a dog, dogs, a teacher.
points: Ask what the listener knows: new, known, or in general.
